original_finding.evidence: The Statement says, “The conformation inequality is an entropy-production statement only under a separate isothermal model that adopts $w$ as its Helmholtz free-energy density … and includes an external thermostat to account for removed heat.” The cited definition describes the thermostat only as a heat reservoir that “maintains $T_0$ and accounts for heat released by this branch.” The Facts and proof derive free-energy dissipation, but provide no entropy-production definition or relation assigning this branch’s dissipation to entropy production. The separate model condition therefore does not specify the thermodynamic link needed for that interpretation.

original_decision.evidence: The original Statement named a Helmholtz density and thermostat but supplied no entropy-production definition or heat/entropy exchange relation; F7 expressly supplies stored-energy dissipation only. The corrected Statement defines C1 volumetric densities e_v,s_v, continuous signed heat-removal h, fixed T0>0, e_vprime=P-h, w=e_v-T0*s_v and pi_s=s_vprime+h/T0. Proof 2.1 now derives T0*pi_s=P-wprime>=0 by differentiation and cancellation. Reddy Chapter 5 equations (5.4.11),(5.4.20),(5.4.23)–(5.4.30) support the adopted conventions. Mechanical conclusions remain unchanged, and the thermodynamic conclusion remains conditional on the additional assumptions.
